idea.title: Is efficiency overrated
idea.summary: Sandstrom and Dunn's 2014 coffee shop study: customers told to chat with the barista felt happier and more belonging than those told to be efficient; closes on a stranger who wants to talk.
hookOptions: Rushing your coffee order is costing you
People who chatted with their barista felt happier
Chat with the barista. Science says so.
I stopped rushing my coffee order
sources: Sandstrom & Dunn (2014), 'Is efficiency overrated?', Social Psychological and Personality Science: coffee shop customers told to have a genuine chat with the cashier vs be efficient; chatters reported more positive mood and belonging.

scenes.say: People who chatted with their barista felt happier than people who rushed.
In 2014, researchers asked coffee shop customers to buy coffee two ways.
One group was told to be efficient, the other to smile, make eye contact and chat.

scenes.sub: the chatters, and they belonged more
scenes.say: The chatters left in a better mood, and felt more like they belonged.
And that was with a barista they'd probably never see again.
